items.stimulus:
Share of Varnhold Speakers Producing the Vowel Merger

| Age group | 2004 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| 18–30 | 41% | 78% |
| 31–50 | 33% | 59% |
| 51–70 | 22% | 36% |
| 71 and older | 15% | 19% |

She interviewed residents in 2004 and again in 2024, recording the share of speakers in each age group who pronounced the pairs the same way. The merger spread fastest among younger residents, but it also advanced among middle-aged speakers: in 2024, the share of speakers aged 31–50 who produced the merger was ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
items.explanation: The statement names two things: the 31–50 row and the 2024 column. Where they cross, the table shows 59%, so that is the value that completes the statement.

A.why: You found the right row but read the 2004 column. The statement asks about 2024.

C.why: You read the 2024 column, but your eye slipped one row down to the 51–70 group.

D.why: You read the 2024 column, but your eye slipped one row up to the 18–30 group, which the passage mentions just before the blank.

items.subtype_name: Read one value from a table or graph
items.stimulus:
Results of Winter Cover Crop Trial

| Winter treatment | Nitrogen retained (kg per hectare) | Weed biomass (g per square meter) |
|---|---|---|
| Crimson clover | 46 | 112 |
| Cereal rye | 71 | 58 |
| Hairy vetch | 52 | 97 |
| No cover crop | 18 | 205 |

Agronomists at a research farm compared four winter treatments to see how well each kept nitrogen in the soil until spring planting. Nitrogen that plant roots do not hold can wash out of fields during winter rains, so a cover crop that retains more of it may reduce the need for fertilizer. The two legumes did less well than cereal rye on this measure but still outperformed bare ground: plots planted with hairy vetch retained ______ of nitrogen per hectare.
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
items.explanation: Find the hairy vetch row and read the nitrogen column. The cell shows 52 kilograms per hectare.

A.why: 71 kilograms is the value for cereal rye, the row just above hairy vetch, not for hairy vetch.

B.why: 97 is in the hairy vetch row, but it comes from the weed biomass column, in grams per square meter. It does not measure nitrogen.

D.why: 46 kilograms is the value for crimson clover, the other legume. You read the wrong row.

P-Wave Arrivals Following the Calder Basin Earthquake

Their records show that the P waves reached the Dunlow station ______ after the earthquake began.

C.why: 34.7 seconds is the arrival time at Ost Harbor, one row below Dunlow.

D.why: 15.9 seconds is the arrival time at Marrow Flat, one row above Dunlow.

A.why: Saline only does have the shortest bar on the graph, but the passage says that group received no adjuvant. You skipped the limiting words 'among the groups whose formulation included an adjuvant' and answered a broader question than the one asked.

D.why: You reversed the comparison. Oil emulsion has the tallest bar at 120, which makes it the highest adjuvant group, not the lowest.

items.stem: According to the graph, which of the following pairings of a meteor shower with its peak hourly count is NOT accurate?
items.explanation: The Perseids bar reaches 80, not 30. The value 30 belongs to the Orionids, the bar just to its right. The other three pairings match their bars exactly.

A.why: The Quadrantids bar does reach 50. If you rejected this pairing, your eye probably moved to a neighbouring bar while you followed the gridline across.

B.why: The Lyrids bar reaches 20, so this pairing is accurate. If you rejected it, you may have checked it against the Orionids (30), the other short bar.

D.why: The Geminids bar reaches 110, so this pairing is accurate. You may have rejected it because 110 seemed too high, or because Ferrante's claim made you suspect it. Her claim isn't part of what you're asked. The graph alone decides.

items.subtype_name: Read one value from a table or graph
items.stimulus:
To compare reinforcement materials for a pedestrian bridge, engineers cast four concrete beams with the same span, depth and concrete mix. The only difference was the material used to reinforce each one. They loaded each beam in two stages and measured how far its midpoint sagged. The project lead hypothesized that, at the heavier design load, only the glass-fiber beam would sag past the 12-millimeter limit.

Midspan Deflection (millimeters)
Reinforcement | 40-tonne load | 60-tonne load
Steel rebar | 10 | 15
Carbon fiber | 8 | 12
Basalt fiber | 11 | 16
Glass fiber | 14 | 21
items.stem: According to the table, which beam's deflection under the 40-tonne load was NOT less than 12 millimeters?
items.explanation: In the 40-tonne column, glass fiber shows 14 millimeters, which is not less than 12. Steel rebar (10), carbon fiber (8) and basalt fiber (11) are all below 12 at that load.

A.why: You read the 60-tonne column, where steel rebar sags 15 millimeters. Under the 40-tonne load the question names, steel rebar sags 10, which is below 12.

B.why: Carbon fiber's 12 is in the 60-tonne column. Under the 40-tonne load it sags only 8 millimeters, the smallest value in that column.

C.why: Basalt fiber's 11 is close to the limit, and it sits directly above the glass-fiber row. If you slipped down a row you would have read 14. Basalt's own 40-tonne value is 11, which is below 12.
